abstract: Becker's Hospital Review (April 2026) documents an 'AI arms race' between payers and providers in revenue-cycle management. Payers use AI to scale claims automation and denials; providers respond with AI-driven documentation, coding, and denial-prevention. Cleveland Clinic reports 15%+ of claims initially denied, requiring appeals to bring the figure below 2%. Revenue cycle teams are entering a new era shaped by AI, intelligent tools, and emerging roles.
keyFindings: RCM AI dynamics: 'become an arms race, and payers are definitely ahead'
Cleveland Clinic: 15%+ of claims initially denied, brought below 2% via appeals
AI-driven denial generation at machine speed creates more appeals workload for providers
Team composition shifting to accommodate AI tools and new AI-oversight roles
Systems like Carle Health cite workforce constraints compounding technological gap
methodology: Journalistic reporting drawing on interviews with health-system RCM leaders.
qualifiers: Narrative reporting rather than quantitative survey. 'Team composition shift' is directional; specific headcount changes are not documented.
